title: Support ticket SLA checker (AI-only run task L2)

content.audience: Synthetic study task for the thesis AI-only run: a support lead checking response and resolution targets
content.problem_statement: Read a support ticket event log and report, for each ticket, how many business minutes its first response and resolution took against the targets of its most urgent priority, and whether each target was met, is pending or was breached. This is a frozen synthetic task for the thesis AI-only run, not a customer product.

user_flows.name: Check targets
steps: Pipe the event log into the CLI
Read each ticket's response and resolution against its targets and the breach count

user_flows.name: Business hours
steps: Log tickets across evenings and weekends
Read times counted in business minutes only

user_flows.name: As of a time and by priority
steps: Read open tickets measured to that time, or only tickets of that priority

user_flows.name: Bad input
steps: Pipe a bad or out-of-order line, or pass a bad argument
Read the error and the exit status

scope: Python 3.8+ standard library only, entry point src/main.py, all code under src

Required structure: a package src/sla with __init__.py and the modules clock, policy, events, tickets, report and cli, each with at least one top-level function (a def at module level; a def only inside a class does not count)
src/main.py imports from sla and each module is imported by main.py or by another module of the package
Run as python3 -I src/main.py, which does not put src on the import path: main.py must add its own directory to sys.path before importing sla

A TIME is D.HH:MM: D is the day number 1 to 99 (one or two digits, not starting with 0), HH 00 to 23 and MM 00 to 59, two digits each. Day 1 is a Monday, so day 6 is a Saturday, day 7 a Sunday and day 8 a Monday again
Business hours are Monday to Friday from 09:00 up to 17:00. The business minutes from time A to time B are the minutes from A up to but not including B that fall in business hours
Read all of stdin and split it into lines on \n, numbered from 1 counting every line. Split each line into whitespace-separated fields; skip a line with no fields or whose first field starts with #

Each other line is an event: TICKET TIME open P, TICKET TIME escalate P, TICKET TIME respond, or TICKET TIME close, with exactly those fields. TICKET is T followed by 1 to 4 digits not starting with 0; P is p1, p2 or p3. Events must be in non-decreasing time order

A line is bad when it does not have that form, its time is earlier than the previous event's, it opens a ticket that was already opened, or it is any other event for a ticket that was never opened or is already closed
For the first bad line print exactly error: line N, print nothing else, and exit 1
Targets in business minutes: first response p1 60, p2 240, p3 480; resolution p1 480, p2 1440, p3 2880. Both are measured from the open event
escalate changes the priority; a ticket's targets are those of the most urgent priority it has had (p1 most urgent), even after a later escalate to a less urgent one
The first response is the first respond event. A close with no respond before it also counts as the first response, at the close time. Later respond events change nothing
The report time is --at TIME if given, else the time of the last event. If --at is earlier than the last event, print exactly error: --at is before the last event and exit 1

For each target: elapsed is the business minutes from open to the response (or close), or to the report time if it has not happened. Status is breached if elapsed is greater than the target, else met if it happened, else pending

Print one line per ticket, in order of the number in its id: TICKET P response E/T STATUS, resolution E/T STATUS, where P is the most urgent priority. Then tickets N, breached M, where N is the number of tickets printed and M how many of them have at least one breached target
--priority P prints only tickets whose most urgent priority is P (the counts cover only those). If no ticket was opened print exactly: no tickets. Each output line ends with \n. Exit 0
Arguments in any order, each at most once: --at TIME and --priority P. Any other argument, a missing or invalid value or a repeated option prints exactly: invalid arguments, then \n, and exits 2
No files, network, environment variables, time zones, clocks or third-party packages

risks.risk: Six tasks written by one author do not establish general build quality
risks.mitigation: Report results only for these frozen tasks, this route, model and role prompts, as the AI-only arm alone

risks.risk: Held-out cases leak to the builder
risks.mitigation: The studio hides held-out studio cases from builder and reviewer; extended cases are never entered into the studio; the repository copy is never sent to runtime roles

obligations: Keep this frozen version unchanged; a change needs a new version and is reported as a deviation
maintenance.review_interval: Not reviewed during the run; frozen until the thesis is submitted
